A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same ECG-text pretraining study, including their appendices. C-MELT corresponds to D-BETA, and Siglep corresponds to ETS. The methods, experiments and supporting material can be matched despite the title and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original full fine-tuning, linear-probing, zero-shot and ablation results for C-MELT, including Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results under D-BETA and adds loss-component ablation results in Appendix A.3, Tables 12–13.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the stated ECG encoder sequence: v1 places positional encoding after the transformer stack and feed-forward projection, whereas v3 places convolutional positional encoding before the transformers. This is a limited change to the architectural specification; it does not establish that the implementation was changed. The four objectives, fusion and N3S are retained, while Siglep becomes ETS.

E1.justification: Both versions pretrain on MIMIC-IV-ECG and evaluate on PhysioNet 2021, PTB-XL, CSN, CPSC2018 and CODE-test. Classification, patient identification, missing-lead evaluation and distribution-shift scenarios are retained. The new loss ablations use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The main comparison tables retain the same baselines. However, v3 Section 4.3 adds MERL to the category-name-only zero-shot comparison accompanying the depth ablation, reporting approximately 62% against the one-layer model's 69.43%. v1's corresponding discussion compares only its layer variants.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 adds GPT-4o-assisted zero-shot controls that remove ETM or jointly remove MLM and MEM on four retained datasets. These supplement the existing category-name-only main ablations. Retained experiments keep their splits, metrics, training fractions and budgets; newly specified masking probabilities are disclosures rather than demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: New Tables 12–13 examine whether ECG-text matching and joint masked reconstruction contribute to zero-shot performance. They extend the existing component, text-encoder and depth ablations. The distribution-shift evaluation, t-SNE analysis and earlier appendix analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 6–8 retain their existing plus/minus reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v3 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 are retained after matching names and reordered columns. New Tables 12–13 add loss-ablation results: for example, MLM/MEM changes PTBXL-Super AUC from 70.3 to 76.2 but PTBXL-Form from 67.4 to 66.1. Section 4.3 also newly reports MERL's approximately 62% category-name-only result. These are additional comparisons, not improved earlier benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same MLM, MEM, ETM and sigmoid contrastive losses; Siglep-to-ETS is a notation change. Neither the main text nor appendices add substantive formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The hybrid-learning, negative-sampling and performance-superiority contributions remain. The abstract now qualifies the 15% improvement as average AUC under 1% training-data linear probing, and the conclusion explicitly claims coverage of over 100 cardiac conditions. These refine the stated scope without introducing a new central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 corrects the depth-ablation interpretation from a language-encoder effect to an ECG-encoder effect. It adds dataset-specific interpretation of ETM sensitivity and discussion of reconstruction's contribution, plus an explanation attributing medical students' higher scores to recent focused training. The earlier N3S and LLM-prompt limitations discussion is largely retained.

D1.justification: v3 discloses lead-masking probability 0.5, input dropout 0.1 and text-encoder fine-tuning during pretraining. It announces sample code and checkpoint availability with an access link, while omitting v1's fairseq-signals framework attribution. Existing optimizer, hardware, preprocessing, downstream hyperparameters and GPT-4o prompt details remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to ETP, ESI, BLIP, ResNet and Song et al.'s ECG foundation-model work. It also emphasizes earlier ECG-text approaches' use of standard ResNet/BERT encoders. The overall hybrid generative–contrastive positioning and critique of MERL remain.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, renames C-MELT and Siglep, edits introduction and method passages, and moves the t-SNE discussion from ablations to experimental results. It adds an impact statement and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout with widespread table and figure repositioning. Figure 2 is redrawn to illustrate N3S selection in Flan-T5 feature space, Figure 1 explicitly marks N3S, Table 2 reorders dataset blocks, and Tables 12–13 are added.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the hybrid objective easier to assess through previously missing ETM and reconstruction controls, and improves reproducibility documentation through masking details, text-encoder training information and a code/checkpoint link. The main benchmark evidence is unchanged. These gains are partly offset by new overstatements: Table 13 contradicts the claim that reconstruction improves every dataset, and unchanged Table 6 does not support the newly explicit 15% full-fine-tuning gain. The net improvement is therefore limited.
